theDestructiveRuleAsImplemented.derived: destructive = sum(newRetirements); destructiveShare = destructive / population, where population is the whole served tier-1 population of the county (not the keyspace). Re-retirements are reported per keyspace and on the run_event and never enter either number.
theDestructiveRuleAsImplemented.why: The writer's loss is the live -> retired transition. Re-stamping an already-retired slice destroys nothing further, and folding it in would let one large previously-retired keyspace mask a genuine new retirement beside it -- and would make a re-run of an old incident look like the incident.
theDestructiveRuleAsImplemented.enforcedBy: the refusal for PUBLISH_RETIREMENT_KEYSPACE_UNACCOUNTED now tests unaccountedDestructive (new retirements on a basis the roll cannot hold) rather than every absence on that basis, so an already-retired keyspace with no index of its own keys no longer refuses a county on every publish forever -- which is exactly the state Williamson is in today and would otherwise have been permanently unpublishable

deviationsDisclosed: CI caught a real defect in this lane's own test changes, and it is disclosed rather than rewritten: at 6bf2a5c the `test` job FAILED (runs 35348784370 and 35348829709). The gate now probes its own reader's existence with the coverage floor's `to_regclass`, and the full-path fake stores did not answer for `cad_property`, so every full-path publish test refused one step early with PUBLISH_RETIREMENT_UNMEASURED instead of reaching the code under test. Fixed in 98c7c9d (the fake answers `to_regclass` for `cad_property`, and only when the scenario actually gives the county a roll, because `retirementRoll == null` must still mean 'no cad_property table' and must still refuse).

HOW IT WAS MISSED, stated precisely because the imprecise version is more flattering than the facts: the defect was NOT invisible locally. BOTH of this lane's local full-suite logs contain it -- P:/tmp/p327-full-tests.txt (the 12:28Z run) and P:/tmp/p327-final-test.txt (the 13:11Z run, the one taken as the final local read) each report 23 failing test locations, 19 of them in test/publish.test.mjs. I read only the P-319/P-320 lines I was looking for (`Select-String -Pattern 'P-319|P-320'`), got five, and reported five. The remaining 14 publish failures were in the log the whole time and are the same single defect. So the honest account is not 'the local run was clean and CI caught something' and not 'local showed five' -- local showed 19 and I read five. A lane that ships a disclosure should ship the one that costs it something; this is it.

The P-319 full-path run_event test asserted the vintage as a literal 2026 while the county under that run is 48021 (declared 2025) and only the roll COUNTS are Williamson's shape. It now resolves the vintage through the same function the gate uses, so the assertion cannot drift from the mirror.
